reviews.title: starter tool kit
reviews.review_text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I received this item for free in exchange for my honest review. The Hyper tough 70 piece project kit comes with a cordless drill, battery, charger, some basic tools and driver bits. It seems fine. For a small handheld drill, it did the job as I was drilling some holes in pvc. The torque seemed fine for this sized drill. It's not going to do much more than basic household projects. It's not as heavy as some of the other drills I've owned, and it feels pretty well-balanced with the battery connected. The other tools also seem to be in the "fine" category. You aren't going to be framing anything with the hammer but if you need to hang a picture it'll work. The needle nose pliers didn't quite cut the wire I tried, the blades need some filing. It however does close with some decent force at the plier end. The tape measure housing is cheap plastic, but seems accurate in measurements. A really nice addition that this comes with is a ratcheting screwdriver. Soap box time: Calling a tool set "70 piece" when 60 of those pieces are driver bits kind of drives me crazy. It's not like it came with 70 tools, yes there are 70 pieces (including the carry case) but it always seems misleading to me for some reason. The battery charger. It works, it's fine. I've seen this a lot in cordless drills and it always ends up being a failure point. The wire between the wall adapter and the charging block is 24 awg. It's very thin. It doesn't need to be thick for the electrical properties, but it will be the first thing to break. When you go to fix it, stripping and splicing that thin a wire can be difficult. I wish manufacturers would at least put 20 awg on it. When it breaks, which it will with even normal wear and tear, you're not going to be able to fix it as they just want you to buy another 70 piece project kit. That being said, this would be something you'd give to your niece as she moves into her first apartment in college.

reviews.title: Just ok
reviews.review_text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] My review is probably more harsh, as I work in the building industry. The drill was not at all powerful and the tools felt cheap overall. I do like the bag though. I will say that for a general household tool set that you won't often use at the price point, this will be fine. Just not tough enough for every day use.
